name: UGC Testimonial Ads
why: Direct testimonial delivery, high trust.

name: UGC Science Backed
why: Creator cites research/studies to back claims.

name: Podcast
why: Mimics a podcast clip/conversation format.

name: Product Comparison Video
why: Side-by-side comparison against a competitor or old method.

name: UGC Listicle
why: Creator runs through a numbered list on camera.

name: Street Interviews
why: Good for cold audiences.

name: UGC Reviews
why: UGC showing the product's benefits. Good for middle of funnel.

name: 5 Reasons Why
why: Good for middle of funnel.

name: Fake Doctor
why: Actor in doctor styling gives a medical endorsement.

name: Talking Objects / Characters / Body Parts
why: Anthropomorphized object or body part narrates the ad.

name: Claymation
why: Stop-motion clay animation, high scroll-stop novelty.

name: Reply To Question
why: Video replying to a real or planted comment/question.

name: Myth Buster
why: Debunks a common misconception in the niche.

name: Crochet Story
why: Story told through a crochet/craft visual metaphor. Pure style, copy-dependent.

name: UGC Testimonial Mashup
why: Multiple short testimonial clips cut together.

name: Personal Story
why: Creator's own story/journey with the problem.

name: Educational UGC
why: Teaches something useful, product woven in.

refs.advertiser: Skin Cupid - Your Korean Skincare Guru

name: Founder Story Ads
why: Personal origin story builds trust and relatability.

name: UGC How-To
why: Creator walks through how to use the product.

name: Product Demo Ads
why: Shows the product in actual use.

name: Reaction / Trend-Hijack (Borrowed Fame)
why: Borrows attention that already exists, disguised as native reaction content.

name: Scenarios
why: Opens on a hypothetical ('imagine if...') to pull cold viewers in.

name: Personal Learning / Epiphany
why: One core lesson: 'wish I knew this sooner.' Product is the lesson.

name: Q&A
why: The question IS the hook. Answer what the buyer is Googling.

name: Day In The Life
why: Native lifestyle content, product appears naturally in-frame.

name: Case Studies
why: Break down one real result with the product as the cause.

name: Levels
why: Level 1, 2, 3 escalation. Product is the top tier.

name: Ranking / Tier List
why: Options ranked against each other; your product lands S-tier.

name: Challenge
why: 'I tried X for 7 days.' Demo-friendly, pairs with before/after.

name: Animated Mechanism Explainer (Clinical VSL)
why: Looks like a med-school explainer, so the claim inherits textbook credibility.

name: AI UGC Avatar
why: 10 hooks cost what 1 used to. Test the script, not the casting.

name: Satisfying B-roll (Front-Splice)
why: Cheapest scroll-stopper test. Buys attention before the ad starts.

name: Breakdown / Explainer
why: Mechanism authority: dissects what happened and why it matters.

name: Personal Update
why: Community/retention for warm audiences who already know you.

name: Goal / Dream Journey
why: Long-arc founder build that keeps people coming back.

name: Lesson From Others (Mentor Story)
why: Borrowed-authority testimonial told in the third person.

name: Episodic Series / Social Show
why: Repeatable content engine. Episodes compound an audience.

name: Win (Victory Announcement)
why: Raw social proof: a milestone the viewer can see is real.

name: Problem-Agitate-Solve
why: Name the problem, twist the knife, resolve with the product.

name: Pack An Order With Me (Fulfilment POV)
why: Owner/POV hands pack a real customer order. Looks like a real small business with orders pouring in, and every product gets a close-up.

name: Stage Talk / Keynote Authority
why: Speaker with a mic on a stage or in a lecture hall. Borrows the stage's authority so the pitch feels like expert teaching, not an ad.

name: Text-Wall Story (Read-Along Still)
why: One still image with a long first-person story on screen. Reads like an organic post; the first line hooks and forces long dwell time.

name: Unboxing (First-Open Reveal)
why: Someone opens the box/packaging and reveals the product for the first time. Anticipation + premium first impression.

name: Try-On Haul
why: One creator tries on several pieces back to back, full-body. Shows fit, range and value in one ad.

name: Celebrity Podcast Clip (Borrowed Authority)
why: Opens on a real clip from a famous podcast (Rogan etc.), then pivots to the product. Borrowed authority stops the scroll.

name: TV Segment Clip (As Seen On TV)
why: Built on a real TV/news segment (anchors, network set, captions). Instant credibility: 'as seen on TV'.

name: Gift Reaction Reveal
why: Camera stays on a real person's face as they open or hear a gift. Emotion sells the gift angle.
